rounds.text: The bear case centers on the persistent structural decay in top-line performance, evidenced by a 3-year compounded sales growth of -6% [E16] and a further trailing twelve months contraction of -4% [E17]. This deterioration is not a brief blip but part of a longer-term stagnation, underscored by a meager 10-year compounded sales growth rate of just 4% [E14] and explicitly flagged by official filings as poor sales growth [E61]. Recent screen data reinforces this downward trajectory, capturing a year-over-year sales decline of 14% [E67] alongside decelerating earnings growth [E68]. While a low price-to-book ratio might invite bargain hunters, this cheap valuation is a direct reflection of a fundamentally declining business model trailing sector tailwinds where the median sales growth sits at 6.3% [E73]. Conceded: the company prints a positive return on assets of 2.92% which outpaces the sector benchmark of -0.73% [E8].
